summary: Sequences are clustered with MMseqs2 at 30% identity and 80% coverage, and whole clusters are assigned to train, validation or test (80/10/10).
methodology: This removes close homologs from the test set but not every distant one, because each sequence joins a single cluster representative. Searched against their training sets, at most 0.1% of similarity-split test proteins have a hit at 90% identity or more and at most 9.3% at 50% or more. Regression targets are standardized on the training split. The ten property tasks have it; the real-case datasets do not.
when_to_use: For performance on enzymes unlike those seen in training, the setting of discovery and engineering. It lowers every PLM's score and reorders them, so rank representations on it.
caveats: Distant homologs remain: 7.9 to 54.6% of test proteins keep a training hit at 30% identity or more. The 30% threshold is a design choice.

citations.title: MMseqs2 enables sensitive protein sequence searching for the analysis of massive data sets
